targets.authors: Driscoll, R., Davis, K. E., & Lipetz, M. E.
targets.title: Parental interference and romantic love: The Romeo & Juliet effect.
targets.evidence_quote: We conducted a replication and extension of Driscoll, Davis, and Lipetz’s (1972) classic longitudinal survey of the Romeo and Juliet effect, wherein they found that increases in parental interference were linked to increases in love and commitment.
targets.outcome_quote: Second, we were able to show that although the more infamous findings of the original study did not recur – interference did not correspond to increased love or commitment – we did replicate the two lesser known findings that interference is linked with poorer outcomes on trust and criticism.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly distinguish failed love/commitment findings and replicated trust/criticism findings from the same original paper. No overall verdict on the whole replication overrides this contrast; absence of the named effect alone concerns one part.

reasoning: Verified matching title, authors and DOI; full nine-page article with references and meta-analysis appendix.
